- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.6) and recent history shows upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (especially <0.4) or shows negative drift, especially after recent spikes.
- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts after sharp price spikes; reduce forecasted overshoot by 10–15% in the immediate 5–7 day horizon.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >15% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment drops below 0.2 in the last 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 5–8% for the next 7–10 days.
- Horizon-specific: for 30-day forecasts, avoid assuming linear continuation; cap forecast at 10–15% below recent 18-day high if sentiment is weak or neutral.
